source.text: וַיֹּסִ֨פוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵה֖וּד מֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And added [the] sons of Israel to do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and Ehud had died.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel again did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and Ehud had died.
en.B: After Ehud had died, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} again did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: After Ehud died, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} once again did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakafanya tena maovu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, naye Ehudi alikuwa amekufa.
sw.B: Ehudi alipokwisha kufa, Waisraeli walifanya tena maovu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Ehudi alipokufa, Waisraeli walifanya tena yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema ni maovu.

es.L: Y volvieron los hijos de Israel a hacer lo malo a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y Aod había muerto.
es.B: Después de que murió Aod, los israelitas volvieron a hacer lo malo a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Después de que murió Aod, los israelitas volvieron a hacer lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho que era malo.

decisions.choice: added to do: did again, went back to doing
decisions.reason: The verb "add" with another verb means doing something once more. Israel returns to the wrongdoing of 3:12, as the cycle of 2:11-19 said it would.

decisions.choice: and Ehud had died: background to the main event, and its cause
decisions.reason: The clause puts the name first and uses a completed verb, which sets the scene rather than moving the story on. The point is that while the judge lived the people held back, and when he died they turned away again, as 2:19 describes. Shamgar (3:31) is not counted here, so this links back to Ehud's eighty years of peace (3:30).

decisions.choice: the evil in the eyes of the LORD: what he judges to be wrong
decisions.reason: "In the eyes of" means "in the judgment of". The evil is named in 2:11-13 and 3:7: serving other gods.

decisions.choice: After Ehud had died, ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the background clause first, so the reader sees at once why Israel went back to its old ways.

source.text: וַיִּמְכְּרֵ֣ם יְהוָ֗ה בְּיַד֙ יָבִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־כְּנַ֔עַן אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָלַ֖ךְ בְּחָצ֑וֹר וְשַׂר־צְבָאוֹ֙ סִֽיסְרָ֔א וְה֥וּא יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בַּחֲרֹ֥שֶׁת הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sold them Yahweh into [the] hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; and [the] commander of his army [was] Sisera, and he [was] living in Harosheth-hagoyim.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sold them into [the] hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; and the commander of his army [was] Sisera, and he [was] living in Harosheth-hagoyim.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sold them into the power of Jabin, king of Canaan, who ruled in Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} handed them over to Jabin, a king of Canaan who ruled from the city of Hazor. The commander of Jabin's army was Sisera. Sisera lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawauza mkononi mwa Yabini mfalme wa Kanaani, aliyetawala huko Hazori; na mkuu wa jeshi lake [alikuwa] Sisera, naye [alikuwa] akikaa Harosheth-hagoyimu.
sw.B: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwauza mikononi mwa Yabini, mfalme wa Kanaani, aliyetawala huko Hazori. Mkuu wa jeshi lake alikuwa Sisera, aliyekaa Harosheth-hagoyimu.
sw.R: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatia mikononi mwa Yabini, mfalme mmoja wa Kanaani aliyetawala kutoka mji wa Hazori. Mkuu wa jeshi la Yabini alikuwa Sisera. Sisera aliishi Harosheth-hagoyimu.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los vendió en mano de Jabín, rey de Canaán, que reinaba en Hazor; y el jefe de su ejército [era] Sísara, y él habitaba en Haroset-goyim.
es.B: Así que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los vendió en poder de Jabín, rey de Canaán, que reinaba en Hazor. El jefe de su ejército era Sísara, que vivía en Haroset-goyim.
es.R: Así que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los entregó a Jabín, un rey de Canaán que gobernaba desde la ciudad de Hazor. El jefe del ejército de Jabín era Sísara. Sísara vivía en Haroset-goyim.

decisions.choice: sold them into the hand of: handed them over to the power of an enemy
decisions.reason: The same picture is used in 2:14, 3:8 and 10:7. God gives his people over to their enemies as one gives up goods in a sale; "hand" means power or control.

decisions.choice: Jabin king of Canaan, reigning in Hazor
decisions.reason: Hazor was the great Canaanite city of the north, above the Sea of Galilee. Joshua 11:1-13 tells of an earlier Jabin of Hazor whom Joshua defeated and whose city he burned; the name may have been used by more than one king of the city. "King of Canaan" calls him ruler of the Canaanites of the region, a stronger title than "king of Hazor".

decisions.choice: Harosheth-hagoyim: a place whose name means "Harosheth of the nations"
decisions.reason: The site is not known for certain. "Of the nations" suggests a district where non-Israelite peoples lived, perhaps in the plain near the Kishon (verse 13). Sisera, whose name is not a Hebrew one, ran Jabin's army from there.

decisions.choice: into the power of
decisions.reason: "Hand" here means power. Balanced keeps the verb "sold" so the reader hears the picture of 2:14, and says "power" so the sense is clear.

decisions.choice: handed them over to
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of "sold ... into the hand of" in plain words.

decisions.choice: "Jabín", "Hazor", "Sísara", "Haroset-goyim"; later "Débora", "Lapidot", "Barac hijo de Abinoam", "Cedes", "el monte Tabor", "el Cisón", "Héber el quenita", "Hobab", "Zaanaim", "Jael"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges: names follow the forms long used in Spanish Bibles, as the terms note for these books sets ("Débora", "Barac", "Sísara", "Jael"). "Barac" is also the form of Hebrews 11:32 in this translation.

source.text: וַיִּצְעֲק֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֠י תְּשַׁ֨ע מֵא֤וֹת רֶֽכֶב־בַּרְזֶל֙ ל֔וֹ וְ֠הוּא לָחַ֞ץ אֶת־בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּחָזְקָ֖ה עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And cried out [the] sons of Israel to Yahweh, for 900 chariots of iron [were] to him, and he oppressed [the] sons of Israel with force twenty years.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for he had 900 chariots of iron, and he oppressed the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel with force [for] twenty years.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because Jabin had 900 iron chariots and had oppressed the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} harshly for twenty years.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help. Jabin had 900 chariots made with iron, and for twenty years he had treated the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cruelly.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana alikuwa na magari ya chuma mia tisa, naye akawaonea wana wa Israeli kwa nguvu [kwa] miaka ishirini.
sw.B: Waisraeli walimlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa sababu Yabini alikuwa na magari ya vita ya chuma mia tisa, naye alikuwa amewaonea Waisraeli vikali kwa miaka ishirini.
sw.R: Waisraeli walimlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awasaidie. Yabini alikuwa na magari ya vita mia tisa yaliyotengenezwa kwa chuma, naye alikuwa amewatesa Waisraeli kwa ukatili kwa miaka ishirini.

es.L: Y clamaron los hijos de Israel {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque él tenía novecientos carros de hierro, y oprimió con dureza a los hijos de Israel [durante] veinte años.
es.B: Los israelitas clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, porque Jabín tenía novecientos carros de hierro y había oprimido con dureza a los israelitas durante veinte años.
es.R: Los israelitas clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} pidiendo ayuda. Jabín tenía novecientos carros de guerra reforzados con hierro, y durante veinte años había tratado con crueldad a los israelitas.

decisions.choice: chariots of iron: war chariots fitted with iron parts
decisions.reason: Chariots were built of wood and leather; "iron" most likely refers to iron fittings, such as tires, axles or plates, that made them strong. In the open plains they gave the Canaanites an army Israel's foot soldiers could not face (1:19; Joshua 17:16-18).

decisions.choice: for: the reason Israel cried out
decisions.reason: The clause explains the cry. Twenty years under a ruler with such a chariot force left Israel no way to free itself.

decisions.choice: oppressed with force: crushed them harshly
decisions.reason: The verb means to press or squeeze, and "with force" stresses how hard the rule was. The same verb is used of Israel's oppressors in 2:18.

decisions.choice: cried out ... for help
decisions.reason: The cry is a call for rescue, as in 3:9 and 3:15. Readable adds "for help" to make that plain.

decisions.choice: Jabin
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he". Balanced and Readable name Jabin, so the pronoun is not taken to mean the LORD.

source.text: וּדְבוֹרָה֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה נְבִיאָ֔ה אֵ֖שֶׁת לַפִּיד֑וֹת הִ֛יא שֹׁפְטָ֥ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽיא׃

records.literal_gloss: And Deborah, a woman, a prophetess, wife of Lappidoth, she [was] judging Israel at the time the that.

en.L: And Deborah, a woman, a prophetess, wife of Lappidoth, she [was] judging Israel at that time.
en.B: Now Deborah, a prophet, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.
en.R: At that time a woman named Deborah was leading Israel. She was a prophet, and she was the wife of Lappidoth.

sw.L: Naye Debora, mwanamke, nabii, mke wa Lapidothi, yeye [alikuwa] akiwaamua Israeli wakati ule.
sw.B: Wakati huo Debora, nabii, mke wa Lapidothi, alikuwa akiwaamua Israeli.
sw.R: Wakati huo mwanamke mmoja aitwaye Debora alikuwa akiwaongoza Israeli. Alikuwa nabii, na mume wake aliitwa Lapidothi.

es.L: Y Débora, una mujer profetisa, esposa de Lapidot, ella juzgaba a Israel en aquel tiempo.
es.B: En aquel tiempo Débora, una profetisa, esposa de Lapidot, juzgaba a Israel.
es.R: En aquel tiempo una mujer llamada Débora dirigía a Israel. Era profetisa y era la esposa de Lapidot.

decisions.choice: a woman, a prophetess: a woman who spoke God's word
decisions.reason: The noun is the feminine form of the word for "prophet", used also of Miriam (Exodus 15:20), Huldah (2 Kings 22:14) and Isaiah's wife (Isaiah 8:3). The word "woman" set beside it is emphatic: the story will turn on what a woman does (verse 9). Deborah speaks for God in verses 6-7, 9 and 14.

decisions.choice: wife of Lappidoth: Deborah's husband was named Lappidoth
alternatives: a woman of torches (a fiery woman)
decisions.reason: The words can be read as "wife of Lappidoth", naming her husband, as Hebrew usually does when it introduces a woman. But the word for "wife" also means "woman", and "lappidoth" is the plural of the word for "torch" (used in 7:16 and 15:4). So it may describe her as "a woman of torches", that is, a fiery, spirited woman. The ending of the name is unusual for a man. Some have also linked "torches" with Barak, whose name means "lightning", but nothing in the text says he was her husband. The text gives no other word about a husband, so either reading is possible; this translation follows the usual pattern of an introduction and reads a name.

decisions.choice: judging Israel: leading Israel and settling its disputes
decisions.reason: On "judge" in this book see 2:16: a leader raised to rescue and govern Israel. The form here describes an ongoing role at that time. Deborah's judging included hearing cases (verse 5), and through her the LORD calls Israel to battle (verse 6).

decisions.choice: a prophet
decisions.reason: English now uses "prophet" for women and men alike. "A woman" is not repeated, since "Deborah" and "wife" already make it plain; the meaning decision keeps its emphasis.

decisions.choice: At that time ...
decisions.reason: Readable starts with the time and splits the description into short sentences.

decisions.choice: "nabii" for the prophetess, with "mwanamke" (a woman) beside it at Literal
decisions.reason: Swahili "nabii" serves for a man or a woman, so no feminine form is needed; the Hebrew already says "a woman" before the title, and Literal keeps both words.

decisions.choice: "profetisa" at every level
alternatives: "profeta" (Spanish also uses the masculine form for women)
decisions.reason: Spanish has a feminine form for a woman who speaks God's word (m1), long used for Deborah and Miriam; the English Balanced "a prophet" says the same thing.

source.text: וְ֠הִיא יוֹשֶׁ֨בֶת תַּֽחַת־תֹּ֜מֶר דְּבוֹרָ֗ה בֵּ֧ין הָרָמָ֛ה וּבֵ֥ין בֵּֽית־אֵ֖ל בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיַּעֲל֥וּ אֵלֶ֛יהָ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: And she [was] sitting under [the] palm of Deborah, between the Ramah and between Bethel, in [the] hill country of Ephraim; and went up to her [the] sons of Israel for the judgment.

en.L: And she [was] sitting under the palm tree of Deborah, between Ramah and Bethel, in the hill country of Ephraim; and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel went up to her for judgment.
en.B: She used to hold court under the Palm of Deborah, in the hill country of Ephraim between Ramah and Bethel, and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came up to her to have their disputes decided.
en.R: She would sit under a palm tree that was named after her, the Palm of Deborah. It was between the towns of Ramah and Bethel, in the hills of Ephraim. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} would come to her there, and she would settle their disputes.

sw.L: Naye [alikuwa] akiketi chini ya mtende wa Debora, kati ya Rama na Betheli, katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu; nao wana wa Israeli wakapanda kwake kwa ajili ya hukumu.
sw.B: Alikuwa akiketi kuamua mashauri chini ya Mtende wa Debora, katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu kati ya Rama na Betheli, nao Waisraeli walikwenda kwake ili mashauri yao yaamuliwe.
sw.R: Alikuwa akiketi chini ya mtende ulioitwa kwa jina lake, Mtende wa Debora. Mtende huo ulikuwa kati ya miji ya Rama na Betheli, katika vilima vya Efraimu. Waisraeli walikuwa wakimjia huko, naye aliwamalizia mabishano yao.

es.L: Y ella se sentaba debajo de la palmera de Débora, entre Ramá y Betel, en la región montañosa de Efraín; y los hijos de Israel subían a ella para el juicio.
es.B: Solía sentarse a juzgar bajo la Palmera de Débora, en la región montañosa de Efraín, entre Ramá y Betel, y los israelitas subían a ella para que resolviera sus pleitos.
es.R: Ella se sentaba debajo de una palmera que llevaba su nombre, la Palmera de Débora. Estaba entre las ciudades de Ramá y Betel, en las montañas de Efraín. Los israelitas iban allí a verla, y ella resolvía sus pleitos.

decisions.choice: sitting: what she did regularly
decisions.reason: The form describes a habit: this was where she usually held court, as judges and elders sat to hear cases (Ruth 4:1-2).

decisions.choice: the palm of Deborah: a landmark tree known by her name
decisions.reason: A single tree could serve as a well-known meeting place. Genesis 35:8 names a tree near Bethel after another Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, but the two are different trees and different women.

decisions.choice: for judgment: to have their cases decided
decisions.reason: Here the noun means a legal decision. People came to her to settle disputes they could not settle themselves.

decisions.choice: the Palm of Deborah
decisions.reason: Capitals show that this is the tree's name, a landmark.

decisions.choice: the towns of
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the towns of" so the names are not mistaken for people or regions.

source.text: וַתִּשְׁלַ֗ח וַתִּקְרָא֙ לְבָרָ֣ק בֶּן־אֲבִינֹ֔עַם מִקֶּ֖דֶשׁ נַפְתָּלִ֑י וַתֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו הֲלֹ֥א צִוָּ֣ה׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֵ֤ךְ וּמָֽשַׁכְתָּ֙ בְּהַ֣ר תָּב֔וֹר וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ עִמְּךָ֗ עֲשֶׂ֤רֶת אֲלָפִים֙ אִ֔ישׁ מִבְּנֵ֥י נַפְתָּלִ֖י וּמִבְּנֵ֥י זְבֻלֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: And she sent and called for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali, and she said to him, Has not commanded Yahweh God of Israel: Go and march to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousands men from [the] sons of Naphtali and from [the] sons of Zebulun?

en.L: And she sent and called for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali, and she said to him, "Has not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, commanded, 'Go, and march to Mount Tabor, and take with you 10,000 men from the sons of Naphtali and from the sons of Zebulun.
en.B: She sent and called for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali. She told him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has given you this command: 'Go, lead the way to Mount Tabor, and take 10,000 men from the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun with you.
en.R: Deborah sent for a man named Barak, the son of Abinoam. He lived in the town of Kedesh, in the land of the tribe of Naphtali. She said to him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, is giving you this order: 'Go to Mount Tabor. Take 10,000 men from the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun with you.

sw.L: Naye akatuma akamwita Baraka mwana wa Abinoamu kutoka Kedesh-naftali, akamwambia, "Je, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, hajaamuru, 'Nenda, ukajipange kwenye Mlima Tabori, uchukue pamoja nawe watu elfu kumi katika wana wa Naftali na katika wana wa Zabuloni.
sw.B: Alituma mtu kumwita Baraka mwana wa Abinoamu kutoka Kedeshi katika Naftali. Akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, amekuamuru hivi: 'Nenda, uongoze watu mpaka Mlima Tabori, uchukue pamoja nawe watu elfu kumi kutoka makabila ya Naftali na Zabuloni.
sw.R: Debora alimtuma mtu kumwita mtu mmoja aitwaye Baraka, mwana wa Abinoamu. Baraka aliishi katika mji wa Kedeshi, katika nchi ya kabila la Naftali. Debora akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, anakupa agizo hili: 'Nenda Mlima Tabori. Chukua pamoja nawe watu elfu kumi kutoka makabila ya Naftali na Zabuloni.

es.L: Y envió a llamar a Barac hijo de Abinoam, de Cedes de Neftalí, y le dijo: «¿No ha mandado {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: “Ve, y marcha al monte Tabor, y toma contigo diez mil hombres de los hijos de Neftalí y de los hijos de Zabulón.
es.B: Envió a llamar a Barac hijo de Abinoam, de Cedes, en Neftalí, y le dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, te da esta orden: “Ve, encabeza la marcha al monte Tabor y lleva contigo diez mil hombres de las tribus de Neftalí y Zabulón.
es.R: Débora mandó llamar a un hombre llamado Barac, hijo de Abinoam. Él vivía en la ciudad de Cedes, en la tierra de la tribu de Neftalí. Ella le dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, te da esta orden: “Ve al monte Tabor. Lleva contigo diez mil hombres de las tribus de Neftalí y Zabulón.

decisions.choice: Has not the LORD commanded? A question that means "the LORD has commanded"
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "yes". Deborah is not asking for information; she is telling Barak what God has ordered, perhaps as a word he has not yet obeyed.

decisions.choice: march: lead out, draw the men up
decisions.reason: The verb means "draw" or "pull". Here it describes leading troops out or spreading them out in order. The same verb is used in verse 7 of God "drawing" Sisera out, so the two sides are drawn to one place.

decisions.choice: Kedesh-naphtali and Mount Tabor
decisions.reason: Kedesh in Naphtali lay in the north of Galilee (Joshua 19:37; 20:7). Mount Tabor is a steep, round hill at the northeast edge of the Jezreel valley, where the tribes of Zebulun, Naphtali and Issachar met (Joshua 19:12, 22, 34). From its slopes foot soldiers were safe from chariots.

decisions.choice: ten thousand: the number of men called up
decisions.reason: On the size of such numbers see the note at Numbers 1. Here the figure is the force raised from two tribes.

decisions.choice: from the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun
decisions.reason: "Sons of" a tribe's ancestor means its members. The men called up are the tribes' fighting men, so Balanced and Readable say "tribes" and need no inclusive wording.

decisions.choice: has given you this command / is giving you this order
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the question into the statement it implies, and keep God's words as a quotation inside Deborah's.

source.text: וּמָשַׁכְתִּ֨י אֵלֶ֜יךָ אֶל־נַ֣חַל קִישׁ֗וֹן אֶת־סִֽיסְרָא֙ שַׂר־צְבָ֣א יָבִ֔ין וְאֶת־רִכְבּ֖וֹ וְאֶת־הֲמוֹנ֑וֹ וּנְתַתִּ֖יהוּ בְּיָדֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will draw to you, to [the] wadi Kishon, Sisera [the] commander of [the] army of Jabin, and his chariots and his multitude, and I will give him into your hand.

en.L: And I will draw out to you, to the wadi Kishon, Sisera, the commander of the army of Jabin, and his chariots and his multitude, and I will give him into your hand'?"
en.B: I will draw Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, out to meet you at the Kishon River, with his chariots and his troops, and I will give him into your hand.'"
en.R: I will lead Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, to the Kishon River to fight you. He will bring his chariots and his soldiers. But I will let you defeat him.'"

sw.L: Nami nitamvuta kwako, kwenye kijito cha Kishoni, Sisera, mkuu wa jeshi la Yabini, pamoja na magari yake na umati wake, nami nitamtia mkononi mwako'?"
sw.B: Nitamvuta Sisera, mkuu wa jeshi la Yabini, aje kukutana nawe kwenye Mto Kishoni, pamoja na magari yake na askari wake, nami nitamtia mkononi mwako.'"
sw.R: Nitamleta Sisera, mkuu wa jeshi la Yabini, mpaka Mto Kishoni ili apigane nawe. Atakuja na magari yake ya vita na askari wake. Lakini nitakuwezesha kumshinda.'"

es.L: Y yo atraeré hacia ti, al torrente Cisón, a Sísara, el jefe del ejército de Jabín, con sus carros y su multitud, y lo entregaré en tu mano”?»
es.B: Yo atraeré a Sísara, el jefe del ejército de Jabín, con sus carros y sus tropas, para que te salga al encuentro junto al río Cisón, y lo entregaré en tu mano.”»
es.R: Yo haré que Sísara, el jefe del ejército de Jabín, vaya al río Cisón a pelear contra ti. Llevará sus carros y sus soldados. Pero yo te daré la victoria sobre él.”»

decisions.choice: the wadi Kishon: the stream that drains the Jezreel valley
decisions.reason: A wadi is a stream bed that may run dry in summer and flood in the rainy season. The Kishon flows west through the plain below Mount Tabor to the sea near Mount Carmel. The Song of Deborah says it swept the enemy away (5:21).

decisions.choice: I will draw ... I will give him into your hand: God himself brings the enemy and hands him over
decisions.reason: The battle plan is God's. He draws Sisera to the place of his choosing, as he drew Pharaoh out after Israel (Exodus 14:4), and the promise "I will give him into your hand" is the regular word of a victory given by God (1:2; 3:28).

decisions.choice: his multitude: his great mass of troops
decisions.reason: The word means a crowd or noisy throng; with the chariots it means the rest of Sisera's army.

decisions.choice: the Kishon River
decisions.reason: "Wadi" is not a common English word. Balanced and Readable say "river"; the meaning decision explains that it was a seasonal stream.

decisions.choice: I will let you defeat him
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of "give him into your hand" in plain words.

decisions.choice: "el torrente Cisón" (L); "el río Cisón" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names a stream bed that fills in the rainy season (m1). Literal says "torrente", the Spanish word for such a stream; Balanced and Readable say "río", as the English says "River".

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ בָּרָ֔ק אִם־תֵּלְכִ֥י עִמִּ֖י וְהָלָ֑כְתִּי וְאִם־לֹ֥א תֵלְכִ֛י עִמִּ֖י לֹ֥א אֵלֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her Barak, If you go with me, and I will go; and if not you go with me, not I will go.

en.L: And Barak said to her, "If you go with me, then I will go; but if you do not go with me, I will not go."
en.B: Barak answered her, "If you go with me, I will go. But if you do not go with me, I will not go."
en.R: Barak answered, "I will go if you go with me. But if you do not go with me, I will not go."

sw.L: Naye Baraka akamwambia, "Ukienda pamoja nami, nami nitakwenda; lakini usipokwenda pamoja nami, sitakwenda."
sw.B: Baraka alimjibu, "Ukienda pamoja nami, nitakwenda. Lakini usipokwenda pamoja nami, sitakwenda."
sw.R: Baraka alijibu, "Nitakwenda ikiwa utakwenda pamoja nami. Lakini usipokwenda pamoja nami, sitakwenda."

es.L: Y le dijo Barac: «Si tú vas conmigo, yo iré; pero si no vas conmigo, no iré.»
es.B: Barac le respondió: «Si tú vas conmigo, iré. Pero si no vas conmigo, no iré.»
es.R: Barac le respondió: «Iré si tú vas conmigo. Pero si no vas conmigo, no iré.»

decisions.choice: two balanced conditions: Barak's going depends on hers
decisions.reason: Barak sets a condition. He does not refuse, but he will not go unless the prophet goes with him. Verse 9 shows that this costs him the honor of the victory.

decisions.choice: the sentence ends with "I will not go"
alternatives: adds: for I do not know the day when the LORD will send his angel to give me success
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text ends here. The early Greek translation adds Barak's reason: that he does not know the day on which the LORD will give success by his angel. That looks like an explanation added later, and the Hebrew is followed. Reviewers should check the evidence.

source.text: וַתֹּ֜אמֶר הָלֹ֧ךְ אֵלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֗ךְ אֶ֚פֶס כִּי֩ לֹ֨א תִֽהְיֶ֜ה תִּֽפְאַרְתְּךָ֗ עַל־הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה הוֹלֵ֔ךְ כִּ֣י בְֽיַד־אִשָּׁ֔ה יִמְכֹּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־סִֽיסְרָ֑א וַתָּ֧קָם דְּבוֹרָ֛ה וַתֵּ֥לֶךעִם־בָּרָ֖ק קֶֽדְשָׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, Going I will go with you; only that not will be your honor on the way that you [are] going, for into [the] hand of a woman will sell Yahweh Sisera. And arose Deborah and went with Barak to Kedesh.

en.L: And she said, "I will surely go with you; only the honor will not be yours on the way that you are going, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will sell Sisera into [the] hand of a woman." And Deborah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
en.B: "I will certainly go with you," she said. "But on the road you are taking, the honor will not be yours, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will hand Sisera over to a woman." So Deborah set out with Barak for Kedesh.
en.R: "Yes, I will go with you," she said. "But the way you are going, you will not get the honor. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will let a woman defeat Sisera." So Deborah went with Barak to Kedesh.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Hakika nitakwenda pamoja nawe; ila heshima haitakuwa yako katika njia unayoiendea, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamuuza Sisera mkononi mwa mwanamke." Naye Debora akainuka, akaenda pamoja na Baraka mpaka Kedeshi.
sw.B: Akasema, "Hakika nitakwenda pamoja nawe. Lakini katika njia unayoiendea heshima haitakuwa yako, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamtia Sisera mikononi mwa mwanamke." Basi Debora aliondoka akaenda pamoja na Baraka mpaka Kedeshi.
sw.R: Akasema, "Ndiyo, nitakwenda pamoja nawe. Lakini kwa njia unayoichagua, hutapata heshima. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamwezesha mwanamke kumshinda Sisera." Basi Debora alikwenda pamoja na Baraka mpaka Kedeshi.

es.L: Y ella dijo: «Ciertamente iré contigo; solo que no será tuya la honra en el camino por donde vas, porque en mano de una mujer venderá {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Sísara.» Y se levantó Débora y fue con Barac a Cedes.
es.B: «Desde luego que iré contigo», dijo ella. «Pero en el camino que emprendes la honra no será tuya, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entregará a Sísara en manos de una mujer.» Así que Débora partió con Barac hacia Cedes.
es.R: «Sí, iré contigo», dijo ella. «Pero tal como lo estás haciendo, tú no te llevarás la honra. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hará que una mujer derrote a Sísara.» Y Débora fue con Barac a Cedes.

decisions.choice: going I will go: I will surely go
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. Deborah agrees at once and without doubt.

decisions.choice: your honor ... on the way you are going: the glory of the victory will not be yours on this undertaking
decisions.reason: "The way you are going" can mean the campaign he is setting out on, or the way he has chosen to act, with conditions. Either way, Barak will not have the honor of killing the enemy commander.

decisions.choice: into the hand of a woman: a woman will defeat Sisera
decisions.reason: A reader expects the woman to be Deborah, but the story will show that it is Jael (verses 17-22). The same verb "sell" from verse 2 is used: the LORD, who sold Israel to Jabin, now sells Jabin's commander.

decisions.choice: on the road you are taking / the way you are going
decisions.reason: Both renderings keep the Hebrew open: the phrase can mean the campaign itself or the way Barak has chosen to go about it.

decisions.choice: will let a woman defeat
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of "sell into the hand of" in plain words.

source.text: וַיַּזְעֵ֨ק בָּרָ֜ק אֶת־זְבוּלֻ֤ן וְאֶת־נַפְתָּלִי֙ קֶ֔דְשָׁה וַיַּ֣עַל בְּרַגְלָ֔יו עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אַלְפֵ֖י אִ֑ישׁ וַתַּ֥עַל עִמּ֖וֹ דְּבוֹרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And summoned Barak Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and went up at his feet ten thousands man; and went up with him Deborah.

en.L: And Barak called out Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and 10,000 men went up at his feet; and Deborah went up with him.
en.B: Barak called out the men of Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and 10,000 men marched up behind him. Deborah went up with him too.
en.R: Barak called the men of Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and 10,000 men followed him. Deborah went with him too.

sw.L: Naye Baraka akawaita Zabuloni na Naftali mpaka Kedeshi, nao watu elfu kumi wakapanda miguuni pake; naye Debora akapanda pamoja naye.
sw.B: Baraka aliwaita watu wa Zabuloni na Naftali waje Kedeshi, nao watu elfu kumi wakapanda wakimfuata. Debora naye akapanda pamoja naye.
sw.R: Baraka aliwaita watu wa Zabuloni na Naftali waje Kedeshi, nao watu elfu kumi wakamfuata. Debora naye alikwenda pamoja naye.

es.L: Y Barac convocó a Zabulón y a Neftalí en Cedes, y subieron a sus pies diez mil hombres; y Débora subió con él.
es.B: Barac convocó a los hombres de Zabulón y de Neftalí en Cedes, y diez mil hombres subieron tras él. Débora también subió con él.
es.R: Barac llamó a los hombres de Zabulón y de Neftalí a Cedes, y diez mil hombres lo siguieron. Débora también fue con él.

decisions.choice: summoned: called out the tribes to war
decisions.reason: The verb means to cry out, and in this form to call people together; it is used for raising troops (6:34-35).

decisions.choice: at his feet: following him, under his command
decisions.reason: To go "at someone's feet" is to follow his lead (8:5; Exodus 11:8).

decisions.choice: the men of Zebulun and Naphtali
decisions.reason: The tribes are named, but it was their fighting men who were called. Balanced and Readable add "the men of".

decisions.choice: Ten thousand
decisions.reason: A number that starts a sentence is written in words.

source.text: וְחֶ֤בֶר הַקֵּינִי֙ נִפְרָ֣ד מִקַּ֔יִן מִבְּנֵ֥י חֹבָ֖ב חֹתֵ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיֵּ֣ט אָהֳל֔וֹ עַד־אֵל֥וֹן בְּצַעֲנַנִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶת־קֶֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Heber the Kenite [had] separated from Kain, from [the] sons of Hobab, father-in-law of Moses, and he pitched his tent as far as [the] great tree in Zaanannim, which [is] near Kedesh.

en.L: And Heber the Kenite had separated from Kain, from the sons of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, and had pitched his tent as far as the great tree in Zaanannim, which [is] near Kedesh.
en.B: Now Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, and had pitched his tent as far away as the great tree in Zaanannim, near Kedesh.
en.R: Now a man named Heber had moved away from the rest of his people, the Kenites. They were descended from Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses. Heber had set up his tent far to the north, by the big tree at Zaanannim, near Kedesh.

sw.L: Naye Heberi Mkeni alikuwa amejitenga na Kaini, na wana wa Hobabu, baba mkwe wa Musa, naye alikuwa amepiga hema lake mpaka kwenye mti mkubwa ulioko Zaananimu, [ulio] karibu na Kedeshi.
sw.B: Basi Heberi Mkeni alikuwa amejitenga na Wakeni, wazao wa Hobabu, baba mkwe wa Musa, naye alikuwa amepiga hema lake mbali, kwenye mti mkubwa ulioko Zaananimu, karibu na Kedeshi.
sw.R: Basi mtu mmoja aitwaye Heberi alikuwa amehama kutoka kwa watu wake, Wakeni. Wakeni walikuwa wazao wa Hobabu, baba mkwe wa Musa. Heberi alikuwa amepiga hema lake mbali upande wa kaskazini, karibu na mti mkubwa ulioko Zaananimu, karibu na Kedeshi.

es.L: Y Héber el quenita se había separado de Caín, de los hijos de Hobab, el suegro de Moisés, y había plantado su tienda hasta el gran árbol de Zaanaim, que [está] junto a Cedes.
es.B: Héber el quenita se había separado de los quenitas, los descendientes de Hobab, el suegro de Moisés, y había plantado su tienda lejos, junto al gran árbol de Zaanaim, cerca de Cedes.
es.R: Un hombre llamado Héber se había ido lejos del resto de su pueblo, los quenitas. Ellos descendían de Hobab, el suegro de Moisés. Héber había puesto su tienda muy al norte, junto al gran árbol de Zaanaim, cerca de Cedes.

decisions.choice: an aside: background the reader needs for verse 17
decisions.reason: The sentence breaks off the story to explain how a Kenite family came to be living in the north, near the battlefield. Its verbs describe what had happened earlier.

decisions.choice: the Kenites, Kain, and Hobab
decisions.reason: The Kenites were a desert clan linked by marriage to Moses, who went with Israel into the land and settled in the south of Judah (1:16). "Kain" is the clan's ancestor's name, used for the whole clan (Numbers 24:21-22). Heber had left them and moved north.

decisions.choice: Hobab the father-in-law of Moses
decisions.reason: The word means a relative by marriage, usually a father-in-law, and 1:16 also calls Moses' father-in-law a Kenite. But Numbers 10:29 calls Hobab the son of Reuel, Moses' father-in-law, which would make Hobab Moses' brother-in-law. The word may cover either relationship, or the family may have had more than one name for its head.

decisions.choice: the great tree in Zaanannim
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text give a slightly different spelling of the place (Zaanaim), and the margin of the text tells readers to say "Zaanannim", the form found in Joshua 19:33, a place on Naphtali's border. The spoken form is followed. The "great tree" was a large oak or terebinth that served as a landmark; Joshua 19:33 may treat the two words together as one name.

decisions.choice: the Kenites
decisions.reason: Balanced names the clan by its usual name instead of the bare ancestor's name "Kain".

decisions.choice: far to the north
decisions.reason: The Kenites lived in the far south (1:16). Readable says where Heber had gone, which the Hebrew "as far as" implies.

source.text: וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לְסִֽיסְרָ֑א כִּ֥י עָלָ֛ה בָּרָ֥ק בֶּן־אֲבִינֹ֖עַם הַר־תָּבֽוֹר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they told Sisera that had gone up Barak son of Abinoam [to] Mount Tabor.

en.L: And they told Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up [to] Mount Tabor.
en.B: Word reached Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up Mount Tabor.
en.R: Someone told Sisera that Barak, the son of Abinoam, had gone up onto Mount Tabor.

sw.L: Nao wakamwambia Sisera kwamba Baraka mwana wa Abinoamu amepanda [mpaka] Mlima Tabori.
sw.B: Habari zilimfikia Sisera kwamba Baraka mwana wa Abinoamu amepanda Mlima Tabori.
sw.R: Mtu fulani alimwambia Sisera kwamba Baraka, mwana wa Abinoamu, amepanda juu ya Mlima Tabori.

es.L: Y avisaron a Sísara que Barac hijo de Abinoam había subido [al] monte Tabor.
es.B: Le llegó a Sísara la noticia de que Barac hijo de Abinoam había subido al monte Tabor.
es.R: Alguien le dijo a Sísara que Barac, el hijo de Abinoam, había subido al monte Tabor.

decisions.choice: they told: a general subject, "Sisera was told"
decisions.reason: No teller is named. It may simply mean that word reached Sisera, though some connect it with Heber's camp in verse 11, close to Kedesh, which explains why that note comes just here.

decisions.choice: Word reached Sisera
decisions.reason: An unnamed "they" means that the news came to him; Balanced says so without naming a teller.

source.text: וַיַּזְעֵ֨ק סִֽיסְרָ֜א אֶת־כָּל־רִכְבּ֗וֹ תְּשַׁ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ רֶ֣כֶב בַּרְזֶ֔ל וְאֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ מֵחֲרֹ֥שֶׁת הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֶל־נַ֥חַל קִישֽׁוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And summoned Sisera all his chariots, 900 chariots of iron, and all the people who [were] with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to [the] wadi Kishon.

en.L: And Sisera called out all his chariots, 900 chariots of iron, and all the people who [were] with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the wadi Kishon.
en.B: So Sisera called out all his chariots, 900 iron chariots, and all the troops who were with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the Kishon River.
en.R: So Sisera gathered all his 900 iron chariots and all his soldiers. He led them from Harosheth-hagoyim to the Kishon River.

sw.L: Naye Sisera akayaita magari yake yote, magari ya chuma mia tisa, na watu wote [waliokuwa] pamoja naye, kutoka Harosheth-hagoyimu mpaka kijito cha Kishoni.
sw.B: Basi Sisera aliyaita magari yake yote, magari ya vita ya chuma mia tisa, na askari wote waliokuwa pamoja naye, kutoka Harosheth-hagoyimu mpaka Mto Kishoni.
sw.R: Basi Sisera aliyakusanya magari yake yote ya vita ya chuma, mia tisa, na askari wake wote. Akawaongoza kutoka Harosheth-hagoyimu mpaka Mto Kishoni.

es.L: Y Sísara convocó a todos sus carros, novecientos carros de hierro, y a todo el pueblo que [estaba] con él, desde Haroset-goyim hasta el torrente Cisón.
es.B: Así que Sísara convocó a todos sus carros, novecientos carros de hierro, y a todas las tropas que estaban con él, desde Haroset-goyim hasta el río Cisón.
es.R: Así que Sísara reunió sus novecientos carros de hierro y a todos sus soldados. Los llevó desde Haroset-goyim hasta el río Cisón.

decisions.choice: summoned: called out for battle
decisions.reason: The same verb as Barak's call to the tribes in verse 10; both sides now gather.

decisions.choice: the people with him: his fighting men
decisions.reason: "People" is often used of an army (5:2; 7:1). The men with Sisera are his troops, beside the chariot force.

decisions.choice: troops / soldiers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "people" means here.

source.text: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ דְּבֹרָ֨ה אֶל־בָּרָ֜ק ק֗וּם כִּ֣י זֶ֤ה הַיּוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁר֩ נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־סִֽיסְרָא֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ הֲלֹ֥א יְהוָ֖ה יָצָ֣א לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַיֵּ֤רֶד בָּרָק֙ מֵהַ֣ר תָּב֔וֹר וַעֲשֶׂ֧רֶת אֲלָפִ֛ים אִ֖ישׁ אַחֲרָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Deborah to Barak, Arise, for this [is] the day which has given Yahweh Sisera into your hand; has not Yahweh gone out before you? And went down Barak from Mount Tabor, and ten thousands man after him.

en.L: And Deborah said to Barak, "Arise, for this [is] the day in which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given Sisera into your hand. Has not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gone out before you?" And Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and 10,000 men after him.
en.B: Then Deborah said to Barak, "Up! This is the day when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given Sisera into your hand. Is it not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who has gone out ahead of you?" So Barak went down from Mount Tabor with 10,000 men following him.
en.R: Deborah said to Barak, "Go! Today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will let you defeat Sisera. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is going ahead of you!" So Barak came down from Mount Tabor, and his 10,000 men followed him.

sw.L: Naye Debora akamwambia Baraka, "Inuka, kwa maana hii [ndiyo] siku ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemtia Sisera mkononi mwako. Je, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakutoka mbele yako?" Naye Baraka akashuka kutoka Mlima Tabori, na watu elfu kumi nyuma yake.
sw.B: Kisha Debora alimwambia Baraka, "Amka! Hii ndiyo siku ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemtia Sisera mkononi mwako. Je, si {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyetoka kukutangulia?" Basi Baraka alishuka kutoka Mlima Tabori, na watu elfu kumi wakimfuata.
sw.R: Debora alimwambia Baraka, "Nenda! Leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakuwezesha kumshinda Sisera. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anakutangulia!" Basi Baraka alishuka kutoka Mlima Tabori, na watu wake elfu kumi wakamfuata.

es.L: Y dijo Débora a Barac: «Levántate, porque este [es] el día en que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha entregado a Sísara en tu mano. ¿No ha salido {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} delante de ti?» Y descendió Barac del monte Tabor, y diez mil hombres tras él.
es.B: Entonces Débora le dijo a Barac: «¡Arriba! Este es el día en que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha entregado a Sísara en tu mano. ¿No es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quien ha salido delante de ti?» Así que Barac bajó del monte Tabor, seguido por diez mil hombres.
es.R: Débora le dijo a Barac: «¡Ve! Hoy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te dará la victoria sobre Sísara. ¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} va delante de ti!» Así que Barac bajó del monte Tabor, y sus diez mil hombres lo siguieron.

decisions.choice: has given: the victory is as good as done
decisions.reason: The verb is completed in form, though the battle has not been fought. Deborah speaks of God's promise as already fulfilled because it is certain.

decisions.choice: the LORD has gone out before you: God marches ahead of his army as its leader
decisions.reason: The picture is of a king leading his troops into battle. The LORD fights for Israel, as in the Song of Deborah (5:4-5, 20) and in Exodus 14:14. The question expects "yes".

decisions.choice: arise: get up and act at once
decisions.reason: The verb means "stand up", used as a call to action, as in 7:9 and 7:15.

decisions.choice: Up!
decisions.reason: A short call to go into action. "Arise" sounds old-fashioned outside the Literal.

decisions.choice: will let you defeat
decisions.reason: Readable puts the certain promise in the future, as an English speaker would say it; the meaning decision explains the Hebrew past form.

source.text: וַיָּ֣הָם יְ֠הוָה אֶת־סִֽיסְרָ֨א וְאֶת־כָּל־הָרֶ֧כֶב וְאֶת־כָּל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֛ה לְפִי־חֶ֖רֶב לִפְנֵ֣י בָרָ֑ק וַיֵּ֧רֶד סִֽיסְרָ֛א מֵעַ֥ל הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֖ה וַיָּ֥נָס בְּרַגְלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And routed Yahweh Sisera and all the chariots and all the camp to [the] mouth of [the] sword before Barak; and went down Sisera from on the chariot, and fled on his feet.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} threw Sisera and all the chariots and all the camp into confusion, by [the] edge of [the] sword before Barak; and Sisera got down from the chariot and fled on foot.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} threw Sisera and all his chariots and all his army into panic before Barak's attack with the sword. Sisera got down from his chariot and ran away on foot.
en.R: As Barak attacked, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Sisera and all his chariot drivers and his whole army panic, and Barak's men cut them down. Sisera jumped down from his chariot and ran away on foot.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamfadhaisha Sisera na magari yote na kambi yote, kwa makali ya upanga mbele ya Baraka; naye Sisera akashuka kutoka garini, akakimbia kwa miguu.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimtia Sisera na magari yake yote na jeshi lake lote hofu kuu mbele ya shambulio la upanga la Baraka. Sisera alishuka kutoka garini mwake, akakimbia kwa miguu.
sw.R: Baraka aliposhambulia, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatia hofu kuu Sisera, madereva wote wa magari yake na jeshi lake lote, nao watu wa Baraka wakawaua kwa upanga. Sisera aliruka kutoka garini mwake, akakimbia kwa miguu.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} llenó de confusión a Sísara y a todos los carros y a todo el campamento, a filo de espada delante de Barac; y Sísara bajó del carro y huyó a pie.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} llenó de pánico a Sísara, a todos sus carros y a todo su ejército ante el ataque de Barac con la espada. Sísara se bajó de su carro y huyó a pie.
es.R: Mientras Barac atacaba, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo que Sísara, todos sus conductores de carros y todo su ejército se llenaran de pánico, y los hombres de Barac los mataron con la espada. Sísara saltó de su carro y huyó a pie.

decisions.choice: routed: threw into confusion and panic
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God throwing an enemy into confusion in holy war (Exodus 14:24; Joshua 10:10; 1 Samuel 7:10). The Song of Deborah tells of the stars fighting and the Kishon sweeping the enemy away (5:20-21), which may describe how this happened.

decisions.choice: to the mouth of the sword: by the sword, with no escape
decisions.reason: A sword is said to "eat", so its edge is its "mouth". The phrase means that the enemy fell by the sword. Here it describes the rout as the work of Barak's swordsmen as well as of the LORD.

decisions.choice: Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot
decisions.reason: The chariots that had made Sisera strong were useless in the rout, perhaps in ground soaked by the Kishon's flood (5:21). The commander leaves his chariot to escape.

decisions.choice: Barak's men cut them down
decisions.reason: Readable makes the sword phrase a clause of its own, saying who used the sword.

source.text: וּבָרָ֗ק רָדַ֞ף אַחֲרֵ֤י הָרֶ֨כֶב֙ וְאַחֲרֵ֣י הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה עַ֖ד חֲרֹ֣שֶׁת הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וַיִּפֹּ֞ל כָּל־מַחֲנֵ֤ה סִֽיסְרָא֙ לְפִי־חֶ֔רֶב לֹ֥א נִשְׁאַ֖ר עַד־אֶחָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And Barak pursued after the chariots and after the camp as far as Harosheth-hagoyim; and fell all [the] camp of Sisera by [the] mouth of [the] sword; not was left even one.

en.L: And Barak pursued after the chariots and after the camp as far as Harosheth-hagoyim; and all the camp of Sisera fell by [the] edge of [the] sword; not even one was left.
en.B: Barak chased the chariots and the army all the way to Harosheth-hagoyim, and Sisera's whole army fell by the sword. Not one man was left.
en.R: Barak chased the chariots and the army all the way back to Harosheth-hagoyim. His men killed every one of Sisera's soldiers. Not one was left alive.

sw.L: Naye Baraka akayafuatia magari na kambi mpaka Harosheth-hagoyimu; nayo kambi yote ya Sisera ikaanguka kwa makali ya upanga; hakubaki hata mmoja.
sw.B: Baraka aliyafuatia magari na jeshi mpaka Harosheth-hagoyimu, na jeshi lote la Sisera likaanguka kwa upanga. Hakubaki hata mtu mmoja.
sw.R: Baraka aliyafukuza magari na jeshi mpaka Harosheth-hagoyimu. Watu wake waliwaua askari wote wa Sisera. Hakuna hata mmoja aliyebaki hai.

es.L: Y Barac persiguió a los carros y al campamento hasta Haroset-goyim; y todo el campamento de Sísara cayó a filo de espada; no quedó ni uno.
es.B: Barac persiguió a los carros y al ejército hasta Haroset-goyim, y todo el ejército de Sísara cayó a espada. No quedó ni un solo hombre.
es.R: Barac persiguió a los carros y al ejército hasta Haroset-goyim. Sus hombres mataron a todos los soldados de Sísara. No quedó ni uno con vida.

decisions.choice: the camp: the army
decisions.reason: The word for "camp" also names the army that camps in it, as in Exodus 14:24.

decisions.choice: not even one was left: the army was destroyed
decisions.reason: The statement is a strong way of saying the defeat was complete. The one man who escapes is Sisera himself, and his escape leads to the next scene.

decisions.choice: Not one man was left / Not one was left alive
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "left" means here.

source.text: וְסִֽיסְרָא֙ נָ֣ס בְּרַגְלָ֔יו אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל יָעֵ֔ל אֵ֖שֶּׁתחֶ֣בֶר הַקֵּינִ֑י כִּ֣י שָׁל֗וֹם בֵּ֚ין יָבִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־חָצ֔וֹר וּבֵ֕ין בֵּ֖ית חֶ֥בֶר הַקֵּינִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And Sisera fled on his feet to [the] tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, for peace [was] between Jabin king of Hazor and between [the] house of Heber the Kenite.

en.L: And Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, for [there was] peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
en.B: Sisera, meanwhile, fled on foot to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, since Jabin king of Hazor and the family of Heber the Kenite were at peace.
en.R: Sisera ran on foot to the tent of a woman named Jael. She was the wife of Heber the Kenite. Sisera went there because King Jabin of Hazor and Heber's family were at peace with each other.

sw.L: Naye Sisera akakimbia kwa miguu mpaka hemani mwa Yaeli, mke wa Heberi Mkeni, kwa maana [palikuwa na] amani kati ya Yabini mfalme wa Hazori na nyumba ya Heberi Mkeni.
sw.B: Wakati huo Sisera alikimbia kwa miguu mpaka hemani mwa Yaeli, mke wa Heberi Mkeni, kwa sababu Yabini mfalme wa Hazori na jamaa ya Heberi Mkeni walikuwa na amani.
sw.R: Sisera alikimbia kwa miguu mpaka hemani mwa mwanamke mmoja aitwaye Yaeli. Yeye alikuwa mke wa Heberi Mkeni. Sisera alikwenda huko kwa sababu Mfalme Yabini wa Hazori na jamaa ya Heberi walikuwa na amani kati yao.

es.L: Y Sísara huyó a pie a la tienda de Jael, esposa de Héber el quenita, porque [había] paz entre Jabín, rey de Hazor, y la casa de Héber el quenita.
es.B: Mientras tanto, Sísara huyó a pie a la tienda de Jael, esposa de Héber el quenita, ya que Jabín, rey de Hazor, y la familia de Héber el quenita estaban en paz.
es.R: Sísara corrió a pie hasta la tienda de una mujer llamada Jael. Ella era la esposa de Héber el quenita. Sísara fue allí porque el rey Jabín de Hazor y la familia de Héber estaban en paz.

decisions.choice: Sisera fled: the story turns back to Sisera
decisions.reason: The name comes first, which shifts attention from Barak's chase to the commander's escape. The verb repeats the end of verse 15.

decisions.choice: the tent of Jael: the women's part of a family's tents
decisions.reason: In a family of tent dwellers a wife could have a tent of her own (Genesis 24:67; 31:33). A man who was not of the family would not normally enter it, so it seemed a safe place to hide.

decisions.choice: peace between Jabin and the house of Heber: a treaty or friendly terms
decisions.reason: The word means well-being and good relations, here an agreement of peace between the king and Heber's family. It explains why Sisera thought he would be safe there, and it makes Jael's choice in verse 21 a choice for Israel against her husband's ally.

decisions.choice: Sisera went there because ...
decisions.reason: Readable puts the reason in a sentence of its own.

source.text: וַתֵּצֵ֣א יָעֵל֮ לִקְרַ֣את סִֽיסְרָא֒ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו סוּרָ֧ה אֲדֹנִ֛י סוּרָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י אַל־תִּירָ֑א וַיָּ֤סַר אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ הָאֹ֔הֱלָה וַתְּכַסֵּ֖הוּ בַּשְּׂמִיכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out Jael to meet Sisera, and she said to him, Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me, do not fear. And he turned aside to her into the tent, and she covered him with the rug.

en.L: And Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said to him, "Turn aside, my lord; turn aside to me; do not fear." And he turned aside to her into the tent, and she covered him with the rug.
en.B: Jael came out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Come in, my lord, come in here with me. Do not be afraid." So he went into the tent with her, and she covered him with a rug.
en.R: Jael came out to meet Sisera. "Come in, sir," she said. "Come into my tent. Do not be afraid." So he went into her tent, and she covered him with a blanket.

sw.L: Naye Yaeli akatoka kumlaki Sisera, akamwambia, "Karibu, bwana wangu, karibu kwangu; usiogope." Naye akaingia kwake hemani, naye akamfunika kwa zulia.
sw.B: Yaeli alitoka kumlaki Sisera, akamwambia, "Karibu ndani, bwana wangu, karibu kwangu. Usiogope." Basi akaingia pamoja naye hemani, naye akamfunika kwa zulia.
sw.R: Yaeli alitoka kumlaki Sisera. Akamwambia, "Karibu, bwana. Ingia hemani mwangu. Usiogope." Basi akaingia hemani mwake, naye akamfunika kwa blanketi.

es.L: Y salió Jael al encuentro de Sísara y le dijo: «Desvíate, señor mío, desvíate hacia mí; no temas.» Y él se desvió hacia ella, a la tienda, y ella lo cubrió con la manta.
es.B: Jael salió al encuentro de Sísara y le dijo: «Entra, señor mío, entra aquí conmigo. No tengas miedo.» Él entró con ella en la tienda, y ella lo cubrió con una manta.
es.R: Jael salió al encuentro de Sísara. «Entra, señor», le dijo. «Entra en mi tienda. No tengas miedo.» Así que él entró en su tienda, y ella lo tapó con una manta.

decisions.choice: turn aside: come off the road and stay
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave one's way and come in, used of accepting hospitality (19:15; Genesis 19:2-3). It is said twice for warmth and urgency.

decisions.choice: my lord: a polite form of address
decisions.reason: Jael speaks to Sisera with the respect due to an important man, which makes him feel safe.

decisions.choice: the rug: a covering, perhaps a blanket or rug
decisions.reason: The word is found only here, and its exact sense is not known. It names something used to cover a person, such as a blanket, rug or heavy cloth.

decisions.choice: Come in
decisions.reason: "Turn aside" means leaving the road to come into the tent; Balanced and Readable say "come in".

decisions.choice: sir
decisions.reason: "My lord" is a polite address here, not a title of rank; Readable says "sir".

decisions.choice: "Karibu" for "turn aside", and "bwana wangu" (L, B), "bwana" (R) for "my lord"
decisions.reason: "Karibu" is the ordinary Swahili word for welcoming a guest in, which is what "turn aside to me" means on Jael's lips; it keeps her hospitality warm. "Bwana wangu" is the polite address to a man of rank; Readable says simply "bwana" (sir).

decisions.choice: "señor mío" (L, B), "señor" (R), with "tú" ("entra", "no tengas miedo")
decisions.reason: Jael speaks politely, as a host speaks to a man of rank (m2). Spanish shows the courtesy in the title "señor", and keeps "tú", since biblical speech in this translation has no polite third person.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלֶ֛יהָ הַשְׁקִינִי־נָ֥א מְעַט־מַ֖יִם כִּ֣י צָמֵ֑אתִי וַתִּפְתַּ֞ח אֶת־נֹ֧אוד הֶחָלָ֛ב וַתַּשְׁקֵ֖הוּ וַתְּכַסֵּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to her, Give me to drink, please, a little water, for I am thirsty. And she opened [the] skin of the milk, and gave him to drink, and covered him.

en.L: And he said to her, "Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty." And she opened the skin of milk, and gave him a drink, and covered him.
en.B: He said to her, "Please let me have a little water to drink. I am thirsty." So she opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him again.
en.R: Sisera said, "Please give me a little water. I am thirsty." Jael opened a leather bag full of milk and gave him some to drink. Then she covered him up again.

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Tafadhali nipe maji kidogo ninywe, kwa maana nina kiu." Naye akafungua kiriba cha maziwa, akamnywesha, akamfunika.
sw.B: Akamwambia, "Tafadhali nipe maji kidogo ninywe. Nina kiu." Basi akafungua kiriba cha maziwa, akamnywesha, akamfunika tena.
sw.R: Sisera alisema, "Tafadhali nipe maji kidogo. Nina kiu." Yaeli alifungua mfuko wa ngozi uliojaa maziwa, akampa anywe. Kisha akamfunika tena.

es.L: Y él le dijo: «Dame a beber, te ruego, un poco de agua, porque tengo sed.» Y ella abrió el odre de la leche, y le dio de beber, y lo cubrió.
es.B: Él le dijo: «Por favor, dame un poco de agua para beber. Tengo sed.» Ella abrió un odre de leche, le dio de beber y volvió a cubrirlo.
es.R: Sísara le dijo: «Por favor, dame un poco de agua. Tengo sed.» Jael abrió una bolsa de cuero llena de leche y le dio de beber. Luego lo volvió a tapar.

decisions.choice: the skin of milk: milk kept in a leather bottle
decisions.reason: Tent dwellers kept milk in containers made of animal skins, in which it soon thickened. Jael gives more than he asked for, the generous welcome of a host; the Song of Deborah adds that she brought curds in a fine bowl (5:25).

decisions.choice: and covered him: covered him once more
decisions.reason: She had already covered him in verse 18. The repeated act shows the care she seems to give him, and sets up what follows.

decisions.choice: a leather bag
decisions.reason: Readable says what a "skin" for milk was.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ עֲמֹ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֑הֶל וְהָיָה֩ אִם־אִ֨ישׁ יָב֜וֹא וּשְׁאֵלֵ֗ךְ וְאָמַ֛ר הֲיֵֽשׁ־פֹּ֥ה אִ֖ישׁ וְאָמַ֥רְתְּ אָֽיִן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to her, Stand [at the] opening of the tent, and it will be, if a man comes and asks you and says, Is there here a man? and you will say, None.

en.L: And he said to her, "Stand [at the] opening of the tent, and it will be, if anyone comes and asks you and says, 'Is there a man here?' you will say, 'No.'"
en.B: He said to her, "Stand at the entrance of the tent. If anyone comes and asks you, 'Is there a man here?' tell him, 'No.'"
en.R: He told her, "Stand at the door of the tent. If anyone comes and asks, 'Is there a man in here?' tell him, 'No.'"

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Simama [penye] mlango wa hema, na itakuwa, mtu yeyote akija na kukuuliza na kusema, 'Je, yupo mtu hapa?' utasema, 'Hapana.'"
sw.B: Akamwambia, "Simama mlangoni mwa hema. Mtu yeyote akija na kukuuliza, 'Je, yupo mtu hapa?' mwambie, 'Hapana.'"
sw.R: Alimwambia, "Simama mlangoni mwa hema. Mtu yeyote akija na kuuliza, 'Je, yupo mtu humu ndani?' mwambie, 'Hapana.'"

es.L: Y él le dijo: «Ponte [a la] entrada de la tienda, y será que, si alguien viene y te pregunta y dice: “¿Hay aquí algún hombre?”, tú dirás: “No.”»
es.B: Él le dijo: «Quédate a la entrada de la tienda. Si alguien viene y te pregunta: “¿Hay aquí algún hombre?”, dile: “No.”»
es.R: Él le dijo: «Quédate en la puerta de la tienda. Si alguien viene y te pregunta: “¿Hay algún hombre aquí dentro?”, dile: “No.”»

decisions.choice: stand: a command to Jael
decisions.reason: The form of the command is the one used for a man, though Jael is a woman. It may be an unusual form, or the plain verb used as a command. The meaning is clear: she is to keep watch at the entrance.

decisions.choice: a man ... a man: anyone, and a man hiding
decisions.reason: The same word is used twice. The first means anyone who might come looking; the second asks whether a man is hiding there. There is irony in his words: when Barak arrives, there is no living man in the tent (verse 22).

decisions.choice: none: "No", there is no one
decisions.reason: The word means "there is not". It is the whole answer Sisera wants her to give.

decisions.choice: anyone
decisions.reason: The first "man" means any person who might come, so every level says "anyone". The second "man" is kept, since the question is whether a man is hiding inside.

source.text: וַתִּקַּ֣ח יָעֵ֣ל אֵֽשֶׁת־חֶ֠בֶר אֶת־יְתַ֨ד הָאֹ֜הֶל וַתָּ֧שֶׂם אֶת־הַמַּקֶּ֣בֶת בְּיָדָ֗הּ וַתָּב֤וֹא אֵלָיו֙ בַּלָּ֔אט וַתִּתְקַ֤ע אֶת־הַיָּתֵד֙ בְּרַקָּת֔וֹ וַתִּצְנַ֖ח בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְהֽוּא־נִרְדָּ֥ם וַיָּ֖עַף וַיָּמֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Jael wife of Heber the peg of the tent, and put the hammer in her hand, and went to him in quiet, and drove the peg into his temple, and it went down into the ground; and he [was] sleeping deeply, and he was weary, and he died.

en.L: And Jael the wife of Heber took the peg of the tent, and put the hammer in her hand, and went to him quietly, and drove the peg into his temple, and it went down into the ground; and he [was] fast asleep and weary, and he died.
en.B: But Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg, picked up a hammer, and crept up to him quietly. She drove the peg through his temple and into the ground. He was fast asleep from exhaustion, and he died.
en.R: But Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg and a hammer. She crept up to Sisera quietly while he lay deeply asleep, worn out. She hammered the peg through the side of his head and into the ground, and he died.

sw.L: Naye Yaeli mke wa Heberi akachukua kigingi cha hema, akatia nyundo mkononi mwake, akamwendea kimya kimya, akakipigilia kigingi katika paji lake, nacho kikazama mpaka ardhini; naye [alikuwa] amelala usingizi mzito, naye alikuwa amechoka, akafa.
sw.B: Lakini Yaeli, mke wa Heberi, alichukua kigingi cha hema, akashika nyundo, akamnyemelea kimya kimya. Akakipigilia kigingi katika paji lake mpaka kikazama ardhini. Alikuwa amelala usingizi mzito kwa uchovu, naye akafa.
sw.R: Lakini Yaeli, mke wa Heberi, alichukua kigingi cha hema na nyundo. Akamnyemelea Sisera kimya kimya alipokuwa amelala usingizi mzito, akiwa amechoka sana. Akakipigilia kigingi kupitia upande wa kichwa chake mpaka ardhini, naye akafa.

es.L: Y Jael, esposa de Héber, tomó la estaca de la tienda, y puso el martillo en su mano, y fue a él calladamente, y le clavó la estaca en la sien, y penetró en la tierra; y él [estaba] profundamente dormido y cansado, y murió.
es.B: Pero Jael, la esposa de Héber, tomó una estaca de la tienda, agarró un martillo y se le acercó sin hacer ruido. Le clavó la estaca en la sien hasta el suelo. Él estaba profundamente dormido por el agotamiento, y murió.
es.R: Pero Jael, la esposa de Héber, tomó una estaca de la tienda y un martillo. Se acercó a Sísara sin hacer ruido mientras él dormía profundamente, agotado. Le clavó la estaca a martillazos por un lado de la cabeza hasta el suelo, y él murió.

decisions.choice: the tent peg and the hammer: the tools for pitching a tent
decisions.reason: Among tent dwellers, putting up the tents was often women's work, so these were tools Jael knew how to use. The Song of Deborah tells the same deed in poetry (5:26).

decisions.choice: in quiet: softly, so as not to wake him
decisions.reason: The word means secrecy or gentleness; here she comes up to him without a sound.

decisions.choice: his temple: the thin side of the head
decisions.reason: The word names the side of the head above the cheek, also in 5:26 and Song of Songs 4:3.

decisions.choice: he was fast asleep and weary: the reason he did not wake
alternatives: and he swooned (or convulsed) and died
decisions.reason: The clause explains how this could happen. The verb for "weary" may instead be read as "he swooned" or "he twitched", describing his death. The plain reading is that he was exhausted, and the text then says simply that he died.

decisions.choice: while he lay deeply asleep, worn out
decisions.reason: Readable moves the note about his sleep before the blow, which is when it applies, and keeps "he died" at the end.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה בָרָק֮ רֹדֵ֣ף אֶת־סִֽיסְרָא֒ וַתֵּצֵ֤א יָעֵל֙ לִקְרָאת֔וֹ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ לֵ֣ךְ וְאַרְאֶ֔ךָּ אֶת־הָאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֣ה מְבַקֵּ֑שׁ וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵלֶ֔יהָ וְהִנֵּ֤ה סִֽיסְרָא֙ נֹפֵ֣ל מֵ֔ת וְהַיָּתֵ֖ד בְּרַקָּתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And look, Barak [was] pursuing Sisera, and went out Jael to meet him, and she said to him, Come, and I will show you the man whom you [are] seeking. And he went in to her, and look, Sisera [was] lying dead, and the peg [was] in his temple.

en.L: And look, Barak [was] pursuing Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him, and said to him, "Come, and I will show you the man whom you are seeking." And he went in to her, and look, Sisera [was] lying dead, and the peg [was] in his temple.
en.B: Just then Barak came by in pursuit of Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. "Come," she said to him, "I will show you the man you are looking for." So he went in with her, and there was Sisera lying dead, the tent peg in his temple.
en.R: Just then Barak came by, chasing Sisera. Jael went out to meet him and said, "Come here. I will show you the man you are looking for." Barak went into her tent with her. There was Sisera, lying dead with the tent peg through his head.

sw.L: Na tazama, Baraka [alikuwa] akimfuatia Sisera, naye Yaeli akatoka kumlaki, akamwambia, "Njoo, nami nitakuonyesha mtu unayemtafuta." Naye akaingia kwake, na tazama, Sisera [alikuwa] amelala amekufa, na kigingi [kilikuwa] katika paji lake.
sw.B: Mara Baraka alifika akimfuatia Sisera, naye Yaeli akatoka kumlaki. Akamwambia, "Njoo, nitakuonyesha mtu unayemtafuta." Basi akaingia pamoja naye, na tazama, Sisera alikuwa amelala amekufa, na kigingi cha hema katika paji lake.
sw.R: Mara Baraka alipita pale akimfuatia Sisera. Yaeli alitoka kumlaki, akasema, "Njoo hapa. Nitakuonyesha mtu unayemtafuta." Baraka aliingia hemani pamoja naye. Kumbe Sisera alikuwa amelala amekufa, na kigingi cha hema kimepenya kichwa chake.

es.L: Y he aquí, Barac perseguía a Sísara, y Jael salió a su encuentro y le dijo: «Ven, y te mostraré al hombre que buscas.» Y él entró donde ella, y he aquí, Sísara [estaba] tendido muerto, y la estaca [estaba] en su sien.
es.B: En ese momento llegó Barac persiguiendo a Sísara, y Jael salió a su encuentro. «Ven», le dijo, «te mostraré al hombre que buscas.» Él entró con ella, y allí estaba Sísara, tendido muerto, con la estaca de la tienda clavada en la sien.
es.R: En ese momento llegó Barac persiguiendo a Sísara. Jael salió a su encuentro y le dijo: «Ven acá. Te mostraré al hombre que estás buscando.» Barac entró con ella en su tienda. Allí estaba Sísara, tendido muerto, con la estaca de la tienda atravesándole la cabeza.

decisions.choice: look: the scene seen through Barak's eyes
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to something seen suddenly. It is used twice: first Barak appears, then Barak sees Sisera dead.

decisions.choice: the man whom you are seeking: Deborah's word comes true
decisions.reason: Barak finds that the enemy commander has already been killed by a woman, as Deborah said in verse 9. The honor of the victory goes to Jael.

decisions.choice: Just then ... there was
decisions.reason: "Look" is put into English by "just then" and "there", which carry the same surprise.

decisions.choice: the tent peg
decisions.reason: "Tent" is added so that the peg is clearly the one in verse 21.

source.text: וַיַּכְנַ֤ע אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא אֵ֖ת יָבִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־כְּנָ֑עַן לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And subdued God on the day the that Jabin king of Canaan before [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And God subdued on that day Jabin king of Canaan before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: So on that day God humbled Jabin king of Canaan before the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: On that day God brought down Jabin, the king of Canaan, and let the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeat him.

sw.L: Naye Mungu akamshinda siku ile Yabini mfalme wa Kanaani mbele ya wana wa Israeli.
sw.B: Basi siku ile Mungu alimnyenyekeza Yabini mfalme wa Kanaani mbele ya Waisraeli.
sw.R: Siku ile Mungu alimshusha Yabini, mfalme wa Kanaani, akawawezesha Waisraeli kumshinda.

es.L: Y sometió Dios en aquel día a Jabín, rey de Canaán, delante de los hijos de Israel.
es.B: Así, aquel día Dios humilló a Jabín, rey de Canaán, delante de los israelitas.
es.R: Aquel día Dios derribó a Jabín, el rey de Canaán, e hizo que los israelitas lo vencieran.

decisions.choice: subdued: brought low, humbled
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone bow down or be brought under. The same word ends the story of Ehud (3:30) and of Gideon (8:28).

decisions.choice: God: the victory is credited to God
decisions.reason: The general word "God" is used here instead of the divine name, but the one meant is the LORD of verses 14-15. The story ends by saying who won the battle.

decisions.choice: brought down ... and let the Israelites defeat him
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what it means for an enemy to be brought low before Israel.

source.text: וַתֵּ֜לֶךְ יַ֤ד בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הָל֣וֹךְ וְקָשָׁ֔ה עַ֖ל יָבִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־כְּנָ֑עַן עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִכְרִ֔יתוּ אֵ֖ת יָבִ֥ין מֶֽלֶךְ־כְּנָֽעַן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And went [the] hand of [the] sons of Israel going and hard on Jabin king of Canaan, until that they cut off Jabin king of Canaan.

en.L: And the hand of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel went on growing harder against Jabin king of Canaan, until they had cut off Jabin king of Canaan.
en.B: And the power of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} pressed harder and harder against Jabin king of Canaan, until they had destroyed him.
en.R: After that, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} kept growing stronger and pressed harder against Jabin, the king of Canaan, until they had destroyed him.

sw.L: Na mkono wa wana wa Israeli ukaendelea kuwa mzito juu ya Yabini mfalme wa Kanaani, hata walipomkatilia mbali Yabini mfalme wa Kanaani.
sw.B: Na nguvu za Waisraeli zikazidi kumlemea Yabini mfalme wa Kanaani, mpaka walipomwangamiza.
sw.R: Baada ya hapo Waisraeli waliendelea kupata nguvu, wakazidi kumshambulia Yabini, mfalme wa Kanaani, mpaka walipomwangamiza.

es.L: Y la mano de los hijos de Israel fue haciéndose cada vez más dura contra Jabín, rey de Canaán, hasta que destruyeron a Jabín, rey de Canaán.
es.B: Y el poder de los israelitas se hizo cada vez más duro contra Jabín, rey de Canaán, hasta que lo destruyeron.
es.R: Después de eso, los israelitas se fueron haciendo cada vez más fuertes y presionaron cada vez más a Jabín, el rey de Canaán, hasta que lo destruyeron.

decisions.choice: the hand went on growing hard: their power grew greater and greater
decisions.reason: "Hand" means power. The verb "go" with another word describes something that keeps increasing. Israel's strength against Jabin grew over time; the one battle began a longer struggle.

decisions.choice: cut off: destroyed, put an end to
decisions.reason: The verb is used of destroying a people or a ruler. It may mean Jabin's death or the end of his kingdom; either way his rule over Israel ended.

decisions.choice: destroyed him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "Jabin king of Canaan". Balanced and Readable say "him" after the full name has just been given.

decisions.choice: the power of
decisions.reason: "Hand" here means power, as in verse 2.
